about.text: The Roaring Meg scheme has two small stations in the Kawarau Gorge between Cromwell and Queenstown, fed from a dam on the Roaring Meg stream, which is said to be named after a gold-rush barmaid. The Otago Central Electric Power Board built the lower station with money advanced by two gold-dredging companies, and it opened in March 1936; workers drilled the rock by hand and hauled the pipes up the hill on a tramline. The upper station, below a concrete arch dam at the head of the valley, followed in 1947 despite wartime shortages, floods and snow.

facts.label: Commissioned
facts.value: Lower Roaring Meg 1936; Upper Roaring Meg 1947
facts.note: the lower station was opened on 19 March 1936; the upper began producing in July 1947

facts.label: River or lake
facts.note: the lower station discharges into the Kawarau River

facts.label: Owner
facts.note: the register's operator is Pioneer Generation, Pioneer Energy's name until 2016

facts.label: Previous owners
facts.value: Otago Central Electric Power Board, 1936–93; Central Electric, 1993–99
facts.note: the board became Central Electric in 1993; Central Electric kept its generation as Pioneer Generation in 1999

facts.label: Stations
facts.value: Lower Roaring Meg (3 MW), Upper Roaring Meg (1.26 MW)

facts.label: Other ratings
facts.value: 4.3 MW (Wikipedia: lower station 3.0 MW and upper 1.26 MW, two turbines each (Elenz uses the EA register's 12 MW))
